newsitem.title: USA: Amoco, Shell Oil form venture in Permian Basin.
newsitem.headline: Amoco, Shell Oil form venture in Permian Basin.

text.p: Amoco Corp. and Shell Oil Co. said Tuesday they agreed to combine their operations in the Permian Basin oil and natural gas fields of west Texas and southeast New Mexico.
The companies said they formed Altura Energy Ltd., a partnership company that will begin operations March 1 as the third largest U.S. independent oil producer.

Amoco will own 64 percent and Shell 36 percent of the venture, which in 1996 had pro forma gross daily production from 6,300 wells of about 170,000 barrels of oil and 220 million cubic feet of natural gas, the companies said.

Altura, Spanish for "height" or "summit", will be headquartered in Houston, with 280 employees here and another 650 workers in the oil and gas fields centred around Midland, Texas, the companies said.

"This is a great day for Altura, Amoco, Shell, and the Permian Basin," said Jim Posey, Altura's president. "I truly believe we have established a solid foundation for this company that will -- as its name implies -- reach new heights in our industry."
The companies said they formed the venture seeking to reduce costs and increase the value of their exploration and production activities in the mature Permian Basin.
Shell Oil, a Houston-based unit of Anglo-Dutch Royal Dutch/Shell Group, and Chicago-based Amoco announced plans for the upstream venture in October 1996.
Talks on the venture stalled late last year, but Amoco executives in recent weeks signalled that a definitive agreement was imminent.
